action: Frank applies for the $2,500 small business stabilization grant that the council is offering to auto-sector businesses with documented revenue decline. His driving school qualifies: it is auto-sector adjacent, it operates under a business license, and his revenue decline is documented and well above the 10% threshold — it is total. He assembles the required documentation: prior year revenue records, business license, a one-page description of the business and its revenue impact from the AV transition. He submits the application online or by hand-delivery to city hall, whichever the process requires. He has all the documentation already because he pulled the requirements in tick 7. He does not exaggerate his situation. He does not minimize it either. He states the facts: he ran a licensed driving school for twenty-eight years, his student enrollment dropped to zero as autonomous vehicle adoption accelerated, and he is actively pivoting to AV literacy instruction. He notes the pivot in the application because it shows he is using the money to rebuild, not just to delay.
